microtheory.name: drives_estimation_control
microtheory.definition: L3 composition pattern — the substrate's drive system + state estimation + corrective control. Composed of: drives with setpoints, Kalman-style state estimators driven by innovations, PID-style correctors with anti-windup, LQR for linear-quadratic regimes, MPC for constrained lookahead, gain scheduling for context-adaptive gains, Ashby's law of requisite variety as the regulator-disturbance match invariant, multi-drive weighted composition, Lyapunov stability as the convergence proof. Each piece exists in other Mts (optimal_estimation_control's Kalman + LQR + MPC; control_systems_foundation's PID + stability; cybernetics_systems' Ashby + homeostasis + feedback; realtime_systems' periodic + WCET); this Mt names how they compose for L3 — the substrate's drive correction surface.

concepts.name: drives_estimation_control_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. Each substrate drive has a setpoint + a state estimator (Kalman-style) that produces an unbiased belief about current state from noisy observations + a corrector that computes a control signal from the error (PID for stable regimes, LQR for linear-quadratic, MPC when constraints matter) + a gain schedule adapting controller parameters per Mt/context + multi-drive weighted composition + Lyapunov-provable stability. Ashby's law constrains the regulator's variety to match the disturbance variety it counters.

concepts.name: drive_with_setpoint
concepts.definition: Component 1. Every drive has (a) a setpoint (target value) + (b) a measurement function over substrate state + (c) a controller. Without all three the drive can't operate as a control loop. Substrate analogue: substrate's drives (curiosity, coherence, parsimony) all need named setpoints + measurement + correction.

concepts.name: error_signal_drive_minus_state
concepts.definition: Component 2. e(t) = setpoint - measured_state. Drives the controller. The sign convention is critical: positive error means substrate is below target, negative means above. Substrate analogue: substrate's ΔF / drive-imbalance signal.

concepts.name: pid_drive_corrector
concepts.definition: Component 3. u(t) = Kp·e + Ki·∫e dt + Kd·de/dt. The default corrector for stable drives. Proportional handles current error, integral eliminates steady-state offset, derivative damps oscillation. PID handles ~95% of industrial loops; suitable for most substrate drives.

concepts.name: anti_windup_integral
concepts.definition: Component 4. Bounds the integral term to prevent saturation during prolonged actuator limits (or basin-locking). Without anti-windup, a drive locked at saturation accumulates indefinite integral that overshoots wildly when the lock breaks. Back-calculation or conditional integration are the standard mechanisms.

concepts.name: kalman_state_estimator
concepts.definition: Component 5. Innovation-driven belief update: ẋ̂ = Ax̂ + Bu + K(y - Cx̂). Substrate uses Kalman-style updates for substrate state (Mt activations, basin depths, drive intensities). Kalman is optimal under linear-Gaussian assumptions; EKF + UKF for nonlinear cases.

concepts.name: innovation_driven_belief_update
concepts.definition: Component 6. Innovation = y - Cx̂ (measurement - prediction). Drives the belief update through the Kalman gain. Innovation distribution is the substrate's principal observation channel — large persistent innovation signals model misfit, not just noise.

concepts.name: lqr_optimal_when_linear_quadratic
concepts.definition: Component 7. When the drive's dynamics are linear + cost is quadratic, LQR (Linear Quadratic Regulator) gives the closed-form optimal feedback K = R^{-1}B^TP via the Algebraic Riccati Equation. Substrate switches to LQR from PID when the drive's regime is provably LQ + computational cost justifies.

concepts.name: mpc_constrained_lookahead
concepts.definition: Component 8. Model Predictive Control. At each tick, solve a finite-horizon optimisation over future control trajectory + apply the first action + repeat. Handles constraints directly (LQR cannot). Substrate uses MPC when constraints matter — admissibility bounds, multi-drive coupling, hard deadlines.

concepts.name: gain_scheduling_per_context
concepts.definition: Component 9. Controller gains (Kp, Ki, Kd; or LQR/MPC parameters) vary per Mt or context — different basins have different sensitivities. A reflex observes substrate context + indexes a precomputed gain table OR adapts via MRAC / self-tuning. The L2 dispatcher's per-Mt hot counters feed this.

concepts.name: variety_matching_principle
concepts.definition: Component 10. Ashby's law of requisite variety: log V(R) ≥ log V(D) - log V(E). Regulator variety must equal or exceed disturbance variety. Substrate's controller-set diversity must match the failure-mode diversity it counters. Without this, regulation is structurally insufficient regardless of parameter tuning.

concepts.name: multi_drive_composition_weighted
concepts.definition: Component 11. The substrate has many drives; they compose as a weighted sum (or Pareto front for hard tradeoffs). Drive weights are themselves controllable. The composition determines which drive wins under contention. Substrate analogue: the drive-weighting mechanism in substrate's current implementation.

concepts.name: lyapunov_stability_check
concepts.definition: Component 12. Substrate state converges iff there exists V(x) > 0 with dV/dt ≤ 0. Used at design time to prove a drive composition is stable. Without a Lyapunov argument, stability is only empirical — not proven. Substrate's Hamiltonian can serve as the Lyapunov function.

concepts.name: drives_converge_to_setpoint
concepts.definition: Invariant. Each drive's state asymptotically approaches its setpoint under nominal disturbance + unchanged setpoint. (Asymptotic stability.) The drive composition + controller choices must satisfy this OR the substrate has a structural drift problem. Lyapunov argument required.

concepts.name: integral_bounded_by_anti_windup
concepts.definition: Invariant. The PID integral term stays within ±I_max even during prolonged saturation. Enforced by anti_windup_integral component. Without this, the substrate would exhibit large overshoot whenever a basin-lock breaks.

concepts.name: variety_matched_to_disturbance
concepts.definition: Invariant. The substrate's regulator-set variety V(R) ≥ V(D). Per Ashby. Implemented by ensuring the controller library has at least as many distinct correction modes as the substrate has distinct failure modes. Without this, some failure mode goes unregulated → drift.

concepts.name: estimator_unbiased
concepts.definition: Invariant. E[innovation] = 0 in steady-state. Persistent bias signals model misfit (substrate's actual dynamics diverge from the Kalman model's assumed A, B, C matrices). Substrate must respond to persistent bias by re-identifying the model, not by re-tuning the gain.

concepts.name: constraints_satisfiable_at_each_tick
concepts.definition: Invariant. MPC's optimisation problem must have a feasible solution at every tick. If feasibility breaks, MPC can't act — substrate must have a fallback (e.g. relaxed-constraint MPC, or revert to LQR). Pre-tick feasibility check + soft constraints handle this.

concepts.name: tradeoff_controller_choice
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: PID (simple, ~95% of loops, no model needed) vs LQR (optimal for LQ regimes, needs model, no constraints) vs MPC (handles constraints, lookahead, expensive). substrate's default: PID for most drives, LQR when LQ-provable, MPC when constraints matter.

concepts.name: tradeoff_estimator_aggressiveness
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: high Kalman gain (trusts measurement, fast response to true changes, noisy in steady state) vs low Kalman gain (trusts model, smooth in steady state, sluggish to true changes). Tuned via Q/R ratio. substrate's default: moderate Q/R; adaptive when innovation distribution shifts.

concepts.name: tradeoff_mpc_horizon
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: long horizon (better lookahead, more compute per tick, larger model error compounding) vs short horizon (cheap per tick, near-greedy, can miss strategic timing). substrate picks horizon ≈ 3-5 ticks for most drives.

concepts.name: tradeoff_drive_weights
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: equal weights (no drive dominates, all progress slowly) vs prioritised (one drive dominates, others lag). substrate uses context-dependent weights — curiosity dominant during exploration phases; coherence dominant during consolidation.

concepts.name: tradeoff_adaptation_rate
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: fast gain scheduling (tracks changing dynamics, can chase noise) vs slow (averages noise, lags real changes). MRAC vs static gain table. substrate picks slow + scheduled rather than fast + adaptive — protects against gain-noise feedback loops.

concepts.name: substrate_rs_canonical_instance
concepts.definition: substrate_rs as canonical. Drives currently implemented as direct rule firings + correction reflexes; L3 pattern is NOT YET fully instantiated as PID/LQR/MPC controllers. The pattern names the design that the existing drive mechanism should generalise to + the AVX-512 / BF16 acceleration noted in commit bc4fe5f's hardware-aware design (Kalman matmul via AVX-512_BF16 at 16 ops/cycle; PID inner loop 16-wide FP32).

concepts.name: hotspot_pgo_as_control_loop_reference
concepts.definition: Java HotSpot's profile-guided optimisation as a control loop. State = method profile. Setpoint = sub-X% interpreter time. Controller = tier-up policy. Innovation = profile vs expected. Reference for adaptive control applied to compilation.

concepts.name: linux_cfs_scheduler_reference
concepts.definition: Linux's Completely Fair Scheduler. State = per-task vruntime. Setpoint = equal vruntime across runnable tasks. Controller = pick min-vruntime. Reference for setpoint-driven scheduling, which substrate's L2 dispatcher mirrors at the reflex level.

concepts.name: tcp_aimd_as_pid_like_reference
concepts.definition: TCP congestion control's AIMD (Additive Increase Multiplicative Decrease) as a PID-like loop. State = cwnd. Setpoint = max throughput without loss. Controller = AIMD. Reference for proportional + reactive control under distributed disturbance.

concepts.name: robot_control_kalman_pid_reference
concepts.definition: Standard robot control: Kalman for state estimation (sensor fusion: IMU + cameras + LIDAR) + PID for joint control. Reference for Kalman + PID composition in a real-time control loop.

concepts.name: adaptive_bitrate_streaming_mpc_reference
concepts.definition: DASH / HLS adaptive bitrate streaming uses MPC: lookahead = next N segments, constraints = buffer occupancy bounds, cost = rebuffer penalty + quality reward. Reference for MPC under hard constraints + soft objectives.

concepts.name: ashbys_homeostat_reference
concepts.definition: Ashby's homeostat (1948). Physical device demonstrating self-regulation under random perturbation. The theoretical predecessor of every drive-corrected substrate. Reference for the variety_matching_principle component + cybernetic stability framing.

concepts.name: naming_completes_l3_design
concepts.definition: Meta. Before this Mt, L3 existed only as a DesignLayer node from the runner-design walk + as scattered control-theory concepts in optimal_estimation_control + control_systems_foundation. There was no name binding 'how substrate drives compose as a control system'. This Mt provides the binding.

concepts.name: this_mt_bridges_drives_to_l2_dispatch
concepts.definition: Meta. L2-dynamic's gain_scheduling_per_context component (in this Mt) reads from L2 dispatcher's per-Mt hot counters. The L2 ↔ L3 bridge is: L2's hot counters provide context observations; L3's gain scheduler uses those observations to adapt controller gains; L3's corrected drives shape what fires next, feeding back to L2.

rules.name: drive_must_have_setpoint_and_measurement
rules.head: Jabberwock declares a new drive
rules.body: the drive must specify (a) a setpoint, (b) a measurement function over substrate state, (c) a controller. Without all three the drive cannot operate as a control loop — it's just a label.

rules.name: integral_must_have_windup_bound
rules.head: Jabberwock implements a PID drive corrector
rules.body: the integral term must have an anti-windup mechanism (back-calculation or conditional integration). Otherwise a basin-locked drive accumulates indefinite integral and overshoots wildly on release.

rules.name: variety_must_match_disturbance
rules.head: Jabberwock adds a regulator
rules.body: the regulator's variety V(R) must equal or exceed the disturbance variety V(D) it counters. Ashby's law. Without this, some failure mode is structurally unregulated.

rules.name: stability_must_be_provable_at_design_time
rules.head: Jabberwock composes drives + corrector
rules.body: the composition must have a Lyapunov argument for stability — V(x) > 0 with dV/dt ≤ 0. Empirical stability isn't enough; design-time proof prevents drift surprises in deployment.

rules.name: estimator_persistent_bias_signals_model_misfit
rules.head: Jabberwock observes Kalman innovation with persistent nonzero mean
rules.body: the response is to re-identify the model (update A, B, C matrices), not to retune gain. Retuning gain on a wrong model produces fast-but-biased estimates; re-identifying produces unbiased estimates.

rules.name: mpc_must_have_fallback_when_infeasible
rules.head: Jabberwock's MPC encounters an infeasible constraint at a tick
rules.body: the substrate must fall back to a controller that has a guaranteed solution (relaxed-constraint MPC, or LQR, or PID). Without a fallback, infeasibility causes the controller to halt — substrate goes uncontrolled at that tick.
